Order 
This application, under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., has been filed for quashment of FIR in Crime No.531/2023 registered at Police Station Bhind Dehat, District Bhind (M.P.) for offences under Sections 304-B and 498A of IPC as well as further proceedings in ST No.13/2024 pending before the Trial Court.
2. Prosecution story, in short, is that upon death of Smt. Preeti Maurya, a Marg Enquiry was conducted.

Statements of witnesses were recorded and it was found that applicant was ill-treating the deceased for want of additional dowry and a car, as a result she was under constant pressure which resulted in death of deceased on account of cardio-respiratory failure.
3.
It is submitted by counsel for applicant that applicant is the husband.

In fact, immediately after marriage, maternal-uncle, brother and mother of deceased were instigating deceased against applicant and were insisting that deceased must initiate proceedings against applicant for recovery of marriage NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22236 2 MCRC-5126-2024 expenses.
When deceased did not agree for the same, then she was beaten by her brother Kuldeep and she was ousted.
Thereafter, deceased started residing in Rithorakalan and had given a handwritten report to the police against her maternal-uncle, brother and mother.
Deceased had gone to her parents home where she suffered acute stomachache and chest pain.

She was immediately shifted to District Chandrakant Mourya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132570401/

sentences.text: Hospital Bhind and ultimately she was shifted to Birla Hospital Gwalior and thereafter she was discharged on 14.05.2023.
After her discharge, applicant and his wife started living peacefully in their house.
On 24.05.2023 brother of deceased took her to Hariom Nagar, Bhind on the ground that Bhandara is organized on 30.05.2023.
He was talking to his wife daily.

On 29.05.2023,
deceased informed him that she has pain in her teeth and accordingly she has taken medicines from doctor.
On 10.06.2023, he was informed by his wife that she went to doctor as she was vomiting and suffering from diarrhea.
On 11.6.2023, he was informed by brother of deceased that deceased is not well and therefore they are taking her to hospital.
Ultimately, he was informed that deceased has been referred to Gwalior.
When he reached Gwalior then he found that deceased was already dead.

Thus, it was claimed by applicant that on account of some poisonous substance given by maternal-uncle, mother and brother of deceased, she had expired.
4.
Heard learned counsel for applicant.

5. Applicant has filed a copy of a representation made to Dy. Superintendent of Police, Bhind (M.P.)
in which aforesaid allegations have been made.

Applicant has also relied upon a handwritten document allegedly NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22236 3 MCRC-5126-2024 wrote by deceased to the SHO alleging against her brother, mother etc.
6.
Whether the aforesaid letter was written by deceased herself or it is a manipulated and a concocted document cannot be adjudicated by this Court while exercising power under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
The allegations made by applicant in his complaint to Dy. S.P. are his defences and the same are required to be proved by applicant before the Trial Court.

Even otherwise in the light of judgments passed by the Supreme Court in the cases of XYZ v. State of Gujarat reported in (2019) 10 SCC 337 , State of Tamil Nadu Vs. S. Martin & Ors. reported in (2018) 5 SCC 718 , Ajay Kumar Das v.
